output.name: Sóleth
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the wind had nothing to carry the sky home. But wind is still wind, and Tavo the Gale was in a good mood. Ennu sewed a white kite for a girl of the Gannet Rocks, who was to marry a goat-keeper across the sound. Her mother tied the tail long, so the ribbons would drag down the cliff to the new door. Tavo lifted it and tore at it, then laughed and set it gently on the roof. The Gulls saw it from above and carried the story up to Vel. Mora the Coat-Changer, white for winter and proud of it, turned to look. Keret the Pole-Runner brought word that one bird was missing from Hesk's count, and Hesk, counting the knots in the tail, said the count was good. So when you see the white kite in the north, do not call it lost. It is a bride's kite, tied to the house it was meant for, and the wind still blesses that door. Mind your knots, and tell the girl to tie her tail long.
output.finding: From Mora, the Coat-Changer, look a hand-span and a finger's width to the south, and there is the white kite.
